Subject: SIG upload: filename/manifest requirements for OneTrust portal

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the SIG questionnaire — our procurement team is ready to accept the package but OneTrust is being particular about file naming and the manifest CSV. Two quick asks: can you confirm (a) whether Redwood will upload a single flattened PDF with all evidence embedded, or if you prefer we upload individual PDFs per control, and (b) the manifest CSV column order for the portal (OneTrust expects filename, md5_checksum, control_mapping, document_type).

We tried uploading a large multi‑doc PDF and OneTrust rejected it with a checksum mismatch; procurement wants an explicit naming convention so their automation can pick it up. If you can send a small sample manifest + the exact filename pattern you plan to use, we can validate on our side.

Attaching the portal error screenshot and the portal instructions PDF from our vendor (see attachments).

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and the error details. We can do either approach but we recommend a single packaged PDF plus a manifest CSV for automation.

Quick answers:
- Upload method: Redwood will prepare a single flattened PDF (SIG_package_v3.pdf) that includes all evidence attachments embedded and a separate manifest CSV (manifest_v2.csv) for the portal.
- Filename pattern: [ACCOUNT]_[YYYYMMDD]_[PACKAGE_VERSION].pdf — e.g., ACME_20270329_v3.pdf. We will include the exact md5 checksum in the manifest under the md5_checksum column.
- Manifest columns we will provide: filename, md5_checksum, file_size_bytes, control_mapping, document_type, upload_path_hint. We understand OneTrust expects a subset; our CSV will include the required headers in that order and extra columns are ignored by their parser.

I'll attach the manifest draft and our internal upload checklist so you can confirm. Marissa — can you double‑check the PDF flattening steps and checksum utility we should run (sha256 vs md5)? Ben — FYI on the portal account and pathing.

Next steps: if you confirm OneTrust will accept md5 in the manifest, we’ll finalize and schedule the upload Wednesday morning PST and share the portal link & checksum. If Whistic or another portal is preferred, let us know and we’ll adapt.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG upload: filename/manifest requirements for OneTrust portal

Vanessa / Ben — quick internal checklist we used last quarter that addresses the common OneTrust pitfalls:

- PDF flattening: print->PDF with fonts embedded, then run qpdf --flatten and then pdfa‑1b conversion if requested by the portal. This prevents form fields from breaking the md5.
- Checksum: OneTrust expects md5 for the manifest import. We compute both sha256 and md5; include both in internal logs, but only md5 goes in the CSV.
- File size limits: keep single file under 500MB; if larger, chunk into ACME_20270329_v3_part1.pdf and _part2.pdf and reference both rows in manifest with the same control_mapping values.
- Filename sanitization: no spaces, use underscores only; remove non‑ASCII chars.
- Upload path hint: include the OneTrust folder ID in upload_path_hint to speed manual routing.

I’ve attached our ot-upload-checklist.txt and a sample script snippet we used to generate the CSV and compute md5 checksums. Will review the final manifest before upload.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex — quick clarification from infra/ops: where do you want the S3 staging path recorded in the manifest? We plan to upload the package to a temporary S3 bucket (s3://redwood-sig-uploads/ACME/ACME_20270329_v3.zip) and then use the OneTrust import UI to pick the files from our side. If OneTrust will pull from a URL, we can provide pre‑signed URLs instead.

We will:
- Generate zipped package: ACME_20270329_v3.zip (contains SIG_package_v3.pdf + evidence files).
- Publish manifest row for each file and include a presigned_url column (if you prefer direct pull).

On the PDF stamping question: we do not add visible stamps (watermarks) unless requested. We can add an audit page with generation timestamp and redwoodinference.com rights statement appended to the PDF; it does not change the md5 of the evidence file if included as a separate appended page — however OneTrust will treat the combined PDF as a single file, so we will compute the checksum after stamping.

Let us know whether OneTrust should ingest via (A) CSV manifest upload + manual file attach, (B) one‑time pre‑signed URL pull, or (C) SFTP (we can stand up temporary SFTP).

Ben
Ben Carter
Cloud Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — appreciate the clear options. Acme procurement confirms:
- Use md5 in the manifest (they will ignore sha256).
- Provide S3 staging path and we will pull via pre‑signed URLs (option B preferred).
- No visible watermarks, please append a one‑page audit summary at the end of the PDF (that’s fine).

Please proceed with the ACME_20270329_v3 package and share the presigned_url columns in manifest_v2.csv when ready. We’ll validate a test upload today and approve for production. DocuSign will follow for the final SIG attestation, but procurement can validate ingestion first.

Onward — Alex
